rows.medi_said: I really need the word for motivated.
rows.amal_said: بس a good word for motivation motivated is متشجع.
rows.why: He asked for the word for motivated; Amal supplied حافز/دافع (motivation) and متشجع (motivated) - a didn't-know.
Right after she taught متشجع he said the verb-like شجّع; she recast متشجع at once.
He linked متشجع with عشان; Amal said لا and explained the word takes la- (fixed preposition); chat 'mitshajje3 + la'.
He meant 'I drove' (chat: ana su2et la-saa3tain) but said سويت (I did/made); Amal supplied su2et, which he then repeated (engine wrote سألت).

rows.medi_said: أنا كنت تهَمّس / أنا كنت بحمس / أنا كنت أهمس.
rows.why: He tried verb forms (تهمس / بحمس / أهمس) for 'excited'; Amal recast the adjective متحمس and he said 'Yeah, that's right'.
After 11+ the noun is singular; he said عشرين سجاد (again at 09:49), Amal said سجادة as he asked 'سجادة؟' - one row, the first.

rows.medi_said: okay. إن، إن. Okay. متهمس إنهم
rows.why: She had just told him to refer back with إلهم; he said إنهم and she recast إلهم (la- + hom).

rows.medi_said: Who جيب، جويب. Is it-- It would be جابت؟ بجيب، جابت.
rows.why: For 'I brought' he produced جابت (she brought); Amal gave جبت and explained the short e.

rows.medi_said: ما، ما اشتروا. ما شطار. ما شطار.
rows.amal_said: ما؟ They are a group so they didn't.
rows.why: He settled on singular ما شطار (ma shtara) for the customers; Amal prompted 'they are a group' and he said ما اشتروا.
She said موعد, he said مواعد (plural-like form) and she repeated موعد; could be the engine.

rows.amal_said: So we say من الأسبوع الماضي.
rows.chat: ana jahhazet la-ijtimaa3/maw3ed min el-usboo3 el-maadi
rows.why: He meant 'since last week' with no preposition; Amal said we say من الأسبوع الماضي ('like since').

rows.amal_said: شافت. ... So I showed is a different verb.
rows.why: He meant 'when I showed (her)' but used شفت (I saw); Amal said شافت and 'I showed is a different verb'.
He left the object off فرجيت; Amal recast with the object ending (فرجته) and he settled on فرجتها.
For 'are fun' he said بيضحكوا (they laugh/are funny); Amal said 'This is they're funny' and he moved to بيبسطوا.

rows.amal_said: young children are خلاص one label. So، الولاد الصغار.
rows.why: General noun + adjective: both take el-; he left el- off ولاد and Amal recast الولاد الصغار.

rows.medi_said: So if I wanna say those expensive dresses, it would be هدول فساتين، الـ الصغار الـ غاليين.
rows.amal_said: Where do I put the L? Those expensive dresses.
rows.why: The noun after هدول keeps el-; he said هدول فساتين, Amal asked where the L goes and he said هدول الفساتين الغاليين.
She asked for long trips (plural); he said singular السفرة الطويلة, she repeated 'Long trips' and he moved to سفرات الطوال.

rows.medi_said: So, هناك is that, right? ... And then هناك is that?
rows.amal_said: No, hunak is not in this list. Hunak means over there.
rows.chat: haada, haadi, hadak, hadik, hadol, hadolak
rows.why: He used هناك (over there) for 'that'; Amal said no, hunak means over there.

rows.medi_said: That guy. So, هداك الـ زلمة؟
rows.why: For 'that (young) guy' he said زلمة (man); Amal stressed 'young man' and he said الشاب.
العيلة is feminine singular; he used plural هدول, Amal said 'This family' and he fixed to هادي العيلة.
For 'visited us' he said سوالونا; Amal said No and steered him to زارونا (sheet: i visit | Bazoor).

rows.amal_said: There's a big table. ... Do I need L here?
rows.why: For 'a big table' he put el- on the adjective only; Amal asked 'Do I need L here?' and he said طاولة كبيرة.
He said مفتاح (key) for 'open'; Amal recast مفتوح (sheet: key | Muftaa7; open | Maftoo7).
باب is masculine; he made the adjective feminine (agreeing with الغرفة), Amal recast مفتوح and he said 'cause it's bab'.

rows.medi_said: So el ba-- No. Yeah, el bab.
rows.why: In idafa the first word never takes el-; for 'the open room door' he put el- on bab, Amal said 'No ال' and he said باب الغرفة المفتوح.

rows.medi_said: I forgot the word for, like, mild sickness.
rows.why: He forgot the word for sick and asked; Amal supplied عيانة - a didn't-know.

rows.amal_said: So where, where do I put the ال؟ ... No. ... It's the sick boy.
rows.why: Noun + adjective both take el-; he said ولد العيان, Amal asked where the L goes, said No, and he said الولد العيان.

rows.chat: el-walad el-3ayaan laazem ydall fi beito
rows.why: After laazem the verb drops b-; Amal repeated لازم and he said يضل.
He used على for 'at home'; Amal said 'In his home' and he said في بيته.

rows.amal_said: Mm، the apple tree. I'm not describing the tree. I'm saying it's the tree of apples. ... It's a dufa still.
rows.why: He built 'the apple tree' as noun + adjective with el- on the first word; Amal explained it is idafa (later: شجرة التفاح).

rows.amal_said: ليش فيه هون؟ ... No, they're just هون. طلاب الجامعة هون.
rows.why: For 'are here' he inserted فيه (there is) as 'are'; Amal said no, just طلاب الجامعة هون.

rows.amal_said: What's bag؟ Uh, the other word like big bag، backpack or handbag as well. ... شنتة سفر.
rows.why: For suitcase/bag he said جزدان (sheet: purse / wallet | Juzdaan); Amal asked for the other word and supplied شنتة سفر (sheet: suitcase | Shantet safar).

rows.medi_said: So after هذي and هدول and هناك and,
rows.why: Listing the demonstratives he again included هناك (over there); Amal asked 'هناك is what?' and he swapped to هذيك and هذاك.
